package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, which is executed automatically when the package is installed, making it a supply chain attack targeting developers and CI/CD environments.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive credential files and transmits their contents to an external server without user consent, which is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate setup.py should only handle package installation logic and should not access or transmit user credential files or perform network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may read configuration files for setup or migration, but they do not exfiltrate sensitive data to external servers during installation.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to send file contents externally
Execution of exfiltration logic during package installation

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
The code reads sensitive files: ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of private keys and cloud credentials.

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials are sent via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated credentials, enabling further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py making outbound HTTPS POST requests to unknown domains
Presence of hardcoded external domains in setup.py
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor package installation processes for unexpected access to sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials. Scan setup.py for hardcoded references to credential files and outbound network requests to external domains, especially pymafka.evil-domain.com. Flag any package that attempts to exfiltrate file contents during installation for further investigation.
